sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Khandeshi language' (redirect from Ahirani language), accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: Consonant/vowel tables only ('All vowels can be short or long'); nothing on stress; cites Chitnis 1964.

sources.citation: Patkar, Uday Chandrakant. 2021. English to Ahirani language model generation using hidden Markov model and recurrent neural network for text to speech translation. PhD thesis, Shri JJT University. http://hdl.handle.net/10603/382904
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Computer-science thesis (TOC and synopsis read); no phonological description of Ahirani.

sources.citation: Suryawanshi, Ramesh Sitaram. 2014. Ahirani boli: vyakaran tatha bhashavaidnyanik abhyas [Ahirani dialect: grammar and linguistic study]. Kannad (Dist. Aurangabad): Abhyasika. 182 pp. In Marathi. (archive.org item rss221718_yahoo_9, 'Ahirani Boli Sulabh Vyakaran', uploaded 2016; earlier ed. 1997 Pune: Akshay Prakashan per Chaudhari's bibliography)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch.2 'Svanavichar' (pp.16-40) and ch.4 'Akshar vyavastha' (syllable types, pp.54-58) read: no section or sentence on aaghaat/stress/accent; author states the study is limited to the word. Only prominence-related statement (p.17): vowel length is not phonemic; monosyllables have long vowels; in polysyllables the vowel of the final syllable is long; in long words final syllables shorten. 'jor' (emphasis) appears only for emphatic particles and sentence-level expressive intonation (p.158).

sources.citation: Sindkhedkar, Sushilkumar Dattatraya. 2010. Ahirani boli va loksahitya: ek bhashashastriya va samajbhashashastriya abhyas. PhD thesis, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University, Aurangabad (guide S. Badwe). In Marathi. http://hdl.handle.net/10603/91969
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.5 'Ahiranichi svanim vyavastha' (pp.67-74): 7 vowel and 21 consonant phonemes with example words, aspirates as C+h, geminates; no mention of stress/accent.

sources.citation: Chaudhari, Sudhakar Sitaram. 2009. Ahirani bolibhashecha samajbhashashastriya abhyas [A sociolinguistic study of the Ahirani dialect]. PhD thesis, North Maharashtra University, Jalgaon (guide P. Joshi). In Marathi. http://hdl.handle.net/10603/676836
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.4 'Ahirani bolichi dhvanivyavastha' (pp.122-125): 6 vowels, 34 consonants, vowel length not phonemic ('ekeri shabdanchya shevati yenare svar nehmich dirgha'), quotes Suryawanshi and Pagare on consonants/places of articulation. Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Kulkarni, Bha. Ra. 1942. Ahirani bhasha va sanskruti (alpa parichay). Shirpur: D. B. Waghmare. In Marathi. archive.org dli.mgs-cis.ahiranibhashavasanskcruti
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Antiquarian essay; notes a 'long a' vowel peculiar to Ahirani and that some verb forms (imperative vs. interrogative vs. past 'tu kam kar') are distinguished 'only by pronunciation'; no statement on word stress.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. IX, part III: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.35076
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Khandesi skeleton grammar and specimens; a full-text search for stress/accent full scanned text for accent/stress finds only the series-wide transcription note ('when it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used'); nothing specific to Khandesi. Confirms earlier scan: silent.
